ui.m.home.t: LYNX SHARE: a lightweight open-source DAW that opens FL Studio and Ableton Live projects
ui.m.home.d: LYNX SHARE is a free, open-source DAW for Windows, macOS and Linux with FL Studio's way of working: Channel rack, Piano roll, Playlist and Mixer. It opens .flp, .als and .flm projects and exports .flp and .als.

ui.why.sub2: What producers keep complaining about in FL Studio, Ableton Live, FL Studio Mobile and BandLab, what LYNX SHARE does about it, and six things that set it apart. Everything here is in the current release.
ui.why.pain.l: These come up again and again on Reddit, the Image-Line and Ableton forums, KVR and app-store reviews. Each answer says where to find it in LYNX SHARE.
ui.why.pain.1.c: One plugin crashes and takes the whole project with it.
ui.why.pain.1.l: Turn on Options › General settings › Run plugins in a separate process, and a plugin that crashes only goes silent. Without it, a plugin that crashes while it plays is switched off and LYNX SHARE keeps running. Either way the plugin reloads from its window, without reopening the project.
ui.why.pain.2.c: A crash, and the last hour of work is gone.
ui.why.pain.2.l: A backup is saved every two minutes and the ten newest are kept for each project. After a crash, the next start offers the newest one, and File › Versions... lists every saved version and backup. Projects are files on your own disk, not in an online account.
ui.why.pain.3.c: FL Studio and Live cannot open each other's projects.
ui.why.pain.3.l: File › Open reads FL Studio projects (.flp), Live 11 and 12 sets (.als) and FL Studio Mobile projects (.flm). File › Export writes .flp or .als, and a report lists what was approximated.
ui.why.pain.4.c: The feature I need is in a higher edition or behind a membership.
ui.why.pain.4.l: There is one edition and it is free. Audio recording, stem extraction, Convert to MIDI, the Clip-launch and Simple workflows and every built-in instrument and effect come in the same download.
ui.why.pain.5.c: Trials that cannot reopen projects, activation limits, logins and ads.
ui.why.pain.5.l: There is nothing to activate or sign in to and there are no ads. Saving, reopening and the number of computers you install it on have no limit.
ui.why.pain.6.c: No Linux version, and FL Studio stopped running under Wine.
ui.why.pain.6.l: LYNX SHARE runs natively on Linux (AppImage and tar.gz) with PipeWire, JACK and ALSA, and loads VST3, CLAP, LV2 and VST2 plugins there. The same project opens on Windows and macOS.
ui.why.pain.7.c: AI features that send my project to someone's server.
ui.why.pain.7.l: Convert to MIDI and Extract stems from sample run on your own computer; stem extraction downloads its model once, after asking. LYNX SHARE has no account. It goes online only for the update check, which you can turn off, a live session you start, or a crash report you agreed to send.
ui.why.pain.8.c: One broken plugin hangs the plugin scan.
ui.why.pain.8.l: Every plugin file is scanned in its own process. A file that crashes or takes too long is marked as failed and skipped, and the Plugin manager can try it again.
ui.why.pain.9.c: Sidechaining takes five steps in the mixer.
ui.why.pain.9.l: Effects with a side input have a "Sidechain from" list of the mixer inserts: pick one and the route is made. Third-party plugins with a second input get the same list.
ui.why.pain.10.c: Moving a mixer track rewires the sends and sidechains.
ui.why.pain.10.l: Moving, inserting or deleting mixer tracks keeps sends, sidechains, automation and MIDI links on the track they belong to.
ui.why.pain.11.c: Heavy instruments use up the computer, and bouncing them loses the way back.
ui.why.pain.11.l: Right-click a channel in the Channel rack and choose Freeze: it plays audio rendered from it and its instrument is unloaded, third-party plugins included. Unfreeze brings back exactly what was there, and Tools › Plugin performance monitor shows which plugin uses the time.
ui.why.pain.12.c: Too many windows before the first song.
ui.why.pain.12.l: View › Layout style › Simple workflow shows one window with the tracks and the timeline, and a first-song tour goes through it step by step. The setup wizard offers it at the first start, and the full windows stay one click away.
ui.why.pain.all: Every complaint and what LYNX SHARE does about it
ui.why.online.l: Work on one project with up to three other people, live or by sending files.
ui.why.online.p1: Send a project. File › Online session › Send project writes a .lynxpack file with the project, its samples and recordings, and an audio render of every part that uses a third-party plugin, so your friend hears it without owning your plugins. They add their part on their own mixer inserts and Playlist tracks and send it back, and you merge it in one undo step. This needs no network, account or server.
ui.why.online.p2: Live session. The host starts a session and shares an invite code. Guests paste it, the host lets them in, and every edit reaches everyone. There is a session chat, guests can follow the host's transport, and the host decides what each person may edit. A part that uses a plugin someone lacks is rendered by the person who has it and streamed to the others as audio.
ui.why.online.p3: Shared plugins. In a live session the host can share plugins with the guests. A shared plugin runs on the host's computer, and a guest uses it in the project and changes its settings from their own window without owning it.
ui.why.online.x1: Four people at most, the host included. Everyone should run the same LYNX SHARE version.
ui.why.online.x2: Live sessions go through the LYNX SHARE relay, end-to-end encrypted with a key taken from the invite code. The relay sees IP addresses and byte counts, not the content.
ui.why.online.x3: A rendered part follows clips you move, but not edits to the notes of a plugin you do not have.
ui.why.online.f2: Opens it, records a part, sends it back
ui.why.online.f3: Merge a part: added in the friend's colour
ui.why.online.cap: From LYNX SHARE 0.1.25: the Online session menu during a live session, the Start live session window and the session chat.
ui.why.projects.t: Opens and writes other DAWs' projects
ui.why.projects.l: FL Studio projects and Ableton Live sets open with File › Open and can be written back.
ui.why.projects.p1: An .flp comes in with its channels, samples, patterns, arrangement, automation and mixer. A Live 11 or 12 set (.als) comes in with its tracks, clips and Session view, which lands in the clip grid. FL Studio Mobile projects (.flm) import the arrangement, samples, drum kits, DW Sampler and DirectWave programs, the Slicer, five of its synths, its effects, its automation and its chord sets. The original file is never changed: saving writes a .lynx file.
ui.why.projects.r1: FLEX packs are never opened. On export, LYNX-only instruments and effects are rendered to audio or swapped for the nearest FL plugin, and modulators are left out.
ui.why.projects.r2: Many of Live's own effects and instruments become LYNX SHARE's own; the ones with no equivalent are dropped and listed. On export, LYNX SHARE's own instruments and effects, effect-parameter automation and insert-to-insert routes are not written.
ui.why.projects.r3: Instruments other than MiniSynth, Transistor Bass, 3x Osc, GMSynth, SuperSaw, DW Sampler, Slicer, DirectWave and the samplers play the built-in synth.
ui.why.projects.cap: After opening a project, the Missing files window says what could not be found and what LYNX SHARE did about each item.
ui.why.fl.t: FL plugins' settings open in LYNX's own engines
ui.why.fl.l: A project that uses FL Studio's native plugins plays without FL Studio installed.
ui.why.fl.p1: FL Studio's own plugins cannot be loaded by another program. LYNX SHARE has its own engine for most of them, written from scratch, and reads each plugin's saved settings from the .flp or from an .fst preset. A Sytrus channel opens as LYNX SHARE's Sytrus engine with the same patch, a Fruity Limiter slot as its limiter with the same values.
ui.why.fl.x1: Not every engine sounds exactly like the original. The plugin list gives each one a status from exact to approximate.
ui.why.fl.x2: Some engines need wave data or samples that belong to FL Studio. LYNX SHARE reads those from your own FL Studio installation and ships none of them.
ui.why.fl.x3: FLEX packs are never opened: a FLEX channel plays the built-in synth instead.
ui.why.fl.cap: LYNX SHARE's own editor for its Sytrus engine.
ui.why.work.l: Patterns and a Playlist by default, a clip grid with scenes or one simple window when you want one.
ui.why.work.p1: The default layout is the pattern workflow FL Studio users know: Channel rack, Piano roll, Playlist and Mixer. View › Layout style › Clip-launch workflow adds a clip grid next to the Playlist, where Playlist tracks are columns and scenes are rows. Clips have launch modes, quantisation, legato, loop and follow actions, and a Grid / Both / Song switch chooses what plays.
ui.why.work.p4: View › Layout style › Simple workflow is for a first song: one window with the tracks and the timeline, a New track chooser that adds a voice, an instrument, a sampler or a starter beat in one click, a track dock with one-knob effects and a Chord pad, and a Finish dock that saves the song as a file. A first-song tour shows the way step by step. The setup wizard offers the three workflows at the first start.
ui.why.work.x1: The clip grid and the Simple workflow are optional. The pattern workflow is unchanged when they are off.
ui.why.work.x2: It is one program with three layouts, not a copy of another DAW: Live's own devices are not there.
ui.why.crash.l: A third-party plugin that crashes does not have to take your project with it.
ui.why.crash.p1: Every plugin file is scanned in a separate process, so a plugin that crashes or hangs during the scan is marked as failed and skipped. With "Run plugins in a separate process" turned on in the general settings, each plugin also runs outside LYNX SHARE while you work: if it crashes, it goes silent, a notice appears and the program keeps running.
ui.why.crash.p2: On Windows, 32-bit VST2 and VST3 plugins run through a bridge that adds no latency. A plugin that crashes in the bridge stops on its own while LYNX SHARE keeps playing.
ui.why.crash.p4: Without a separate process, a plugin that crashes while it plays is switched off and LYNX SHARE keeps running, on Windows, macOS and Linux. A plugin that crashes while a project loads is left out, and the project opens with its settings kept.
ui.why.crash.x1: Running plugins in a separate process is off by default. You can turn it on for everything or for one plugin.
ui.why.crash.x2: A plugin in a separate process, or in the 32-bit bridge, opens its editor in its own window.
ui.why.crash.x4: On Linux and macOS, without a separate process, a crash while a plugin opens its editor, loads a preset or works on its own threads is not caught yet.
ui.why.crash.cap: The lower part of the Plugin manager in 0.1.25, with its note that each plugin file is examined in a separate process.
ui.why.free.t: Free on Windows, Linux and macOS
ui.why.free.l: No price, no account, no subscription, and the source is public.
ui.why.free.p1: LYNX SHARE runs on Windows 10 and 11, on macOS 11 or newer (Apple Silicon and Intel) and on Linux x86_64. The same project file opens on all three. It is licensed under the AGPL-3.0: you can read the code, build it yourself and change it.
ui.why.free.p2: It does not ask you to sign in, and it sends nothing over the network unless you ask it to: checking for updates, a live session, or a crash report you agreed to send.
ui.why.free.x1: It is an alpha. Expect bugs and keep backups.
ui.why.free.x2: The Windows build is not code-signed and the macOS build is not notarized yet, so both systems warn the first time you open it.
ui.why.free.x3: The macOS build is made by CI and has had little testing on real Macs.

ui.why.work.alt: The Clip-launch layout: a clip grid with scenes next to the Playlist
ui.hero.pill: Free & open source · Windows · macOS · Linux
ui.home.lead: LYNX SHARE is a DAW that works the way FL Studio does: Channel rack, Piano roll, Playlist and Mixer, with the same shortcuts. It opens FL Studio projects (.flp), Ableton Live sets (.als) and FL Studio Mobile projects (.flm), and exports .flp and .als back. It is free under the AGPL-3.0 and still an alpha.
ui.home.what1: You build patterns in the Channel rack and the Piano roll, arrange them with audio and automation clips in the Playlist, and mix in the Mixer: up to 127 insert tracks with 10 effect slots each, sends and sidechain. If you know FL Studio, the windows, mouse gestures and shortcuts are where you expect them.
ui.home.what2: Projects from other programs open directly. An .flp comes in with its channels, samples, patterns, arrangement, automation and mixer, and FL Studio's native plugins are replaced by LYNX SHARE's own engines. Live 11 and 12 sets open too, and their Session clips land in an optional clip grid with scenes. The same menu (View › Layout style) has a Simple workflow: one window for a first song.
ui.home.what3: Third-party plugins load as VST3 and CLAP on every system, plus Audio Units on macOS and LV2 on Linux. VST2 plugins load on Windows and Linux, and on Windows 32-bit plugins run through a bridge.
ui.home.miss: It is an alpha, so expect bugs and keep backups. Not every FL Studio plugin is recreated exactly: the plugin list gives the status of each one. Only some of Live's own devices are converted, and in .flm projects only some of FL Studio Mobile's instruments are recreated. The Windows build is not code-signed and the macOS build is not notarized yet, so both systems warn the first time you open it.

ui.home.capPr: Piano roll. Notes, slides, chords and scales, with velocity and pitch lanes.
ui.home.capMx: Mixer. Inserts, sends, sidechain and delay compensation.

ui.home.src1: LYNX SHARE is written in C++20 with JUCE 8. The code, the tests and the notes on every FL Studio behaviour it reproduces are in one public repository. FL Studio and Live were studied from the outside and the code was written from scratch: nothing from Image-Line or Ableton is in it.
ui.home.src2: Bug reports and pull requests are welcome. Several fixes in recent releases came from users.
ui.home.comm1: Discord: chat, help, feedback and release announcements.
ui.home.comm2: Radiant is an independent, unofficial Android adaptation of LYNX SHARE for tablets and phones. It is a separate community project, not an official LYNX SHARE release, and it is not maintained or reviewed by us.
ui.home.srcN: Build instructions for each system are in docs/SETUP_DEV.md.
ui.sup.p1: LYNX SHARE is free and open source, made by an independent developer. Donations keep the project going: they pay for the server behind sharing, the relay and the tests, the AI tools used in development, this website, the Apple developer account for signed Mac builds, and the reference plugins used to check the sound quality.
ui.sup.p2: Donating is optional and never unlocks anything. Everything in LYNX SHARE stays free for everyone.
ui.sig.title: Code signing policy
ui.sig.p1: Free code signing provided by SignPath.io, certificate by SignPath Foundation.
ui.sig.p2: Release files are built from the public source by GitHub Actions, and every signing request is approved by hand.
ui.sig.roles: Authors, reviewers and approvers: Ka1-S (repository owner).
ui.sig.pp: This program will not transfer any information to other networked systems unless specifically requested by the user or the person installing or operating it. Privacy policy
ui.sig.cr2: Opt-in only. After a crash or freeze LYNX SHARE asks before sending a report (Settings › General › Crash reports: Ask / Always send / Never send). A report holds a random id, the LYNX SHARE version, the operating system, CPU, graphics cards and drivers, screen size, audio device and settings, the crash or freeze file, the session's last 60 steps, and the names and versions of the third-party plugins that were loaded. User names in paths become <user>, and file names are left out unless you tick "include file names". No audio, projects or samples, no machine name and no IP address are stored. Reports are used only to fix bugs. To have one deleted, open an issue with its id (LYNX SHARE shows it after sending; every sent id is also listed in crash-reports/sent.log in LYNX SHARE's settings folder).

ui.fe.sub: What is in the current release, window by window, and where it still falls short. The wiki explains how to use each part.
ui.fe.winL: The layout follows FL Studio: Browser, Channel rack, Piano roll, Playlist and Mixer, each opened and closed with the same keys as there.
ui.fe.plP: Pattern, audio and automation clips on tracks. Right-click a clip for split, chop, merge, reverse, normalize and fit to tempo.
ui.fe.plA: Several arrangements in one project, markers and time selection
ui.fe.plB: Automation clips with curves for any knob or fader, and optional automation lanes under tracks
ui.fe.plC: Audio recording with loop takes and comping
ui.fe.plD: Video tracks with a timecode ruler (export with video needs FFmpeg)
ui.fe.plE: Warp markers and Auto-warp, to lock audio clips to the beat
ui.fe.plF: FL Studio's 13 automation curve modes on every point
ui.fe.crP: A step sequencer with one row per instrument. Each channel has volume, pan, mute and solo, and each pattern its own name, colour and length.
ui.fe.crA: Swing, cut groups, an arpeggiator and layer channels
ui.fe.crB: The PC keyboard plays notes like a piano
ui.fe.crC: Freeze: a channel plays as audio and its instrument is unloaded
ui.fe.prP: Configurable snap, chords and scales, 16 note colours, note groups, and slide and porta notes.
ui.fe.prA: Lanes for velocity, pan and pitch under the notes
ui.fe.prC: Quantize, strum, arpeggiate and randomize tools
ui.fe.prE: Note chance, velocity range and Piano roll scripts
ui.fe.prF: Limit to a scale or chord, Scale levels, Flip and Randomize, as in FL Studio
ui.fe.mxP: Up to 127 insert tracks. Each has 10 effect slots with dry/wet, sends with levels, a built-in EQ and delay compensation.
ui.fe.mxA: Sidechain from one menu on any effect with a side input
ui.fe.mxB: VCA faders and groups that fold
ui.fe.mxC: Moving a track keeps its sends, sidechains and automation
ui.fe.mxD: An optional loudness meter (LUFS and true peak) beside the Master
ui.fe.mxE: Edison on any mixer slot, recording even with its window closed
ui.fe.auP: Any knob or fader of a channel, the mixer, an effect or a plugin can become a clip with points and curves. MIDI controllers can be linked to any parameter, and modulators (an LFO or a random source) move a knob around its own value.
ui.fe.auP2: Common MIDI controllers work from profiles (Mackie Control, Launchkey MK3, APC Key 25 mk2, KeyLab Essential mk3 and nanoKONTROL2). An MPE controller plays each note with its own bend, timbre and pressure; this is a first stage. Right-click a control › Link to controller... opens Remote control settings, as in FL Studio, for knobs, notes and buttons.
ui.fe.clP: An optional layout (View › Layout style) puts a grid of clips and scenes next to the Playlist, in the manner of Ableton Live's Session view. Clips have launch modes, quantisation, legato, loop and follow actions.
ui.fe.clP2: Live sets bring their Session clips into this grid, and exporting an .als writes the grid back. The pattern layout stays the default and nothing changes in it.
ui.fe.clP3: A selected clip opens in a Clip View with Clip, Launch and Notes panels and Live 12's MIDI tools. The selected track's effects show as a chain of cards, and racks with chains, zones and macros open from Live sets and are written back. A Session mixer sits under the grid, a Drum Rack plays pads with choke groups and return chains, and MIDI and Key Map Modes link controllers and computer keys to clips, scenes and knobs.
ui.fe.simP: The same menu has a third layout, the Simple workflow, for a first song: one window with the tracks and the timeline, a New track chooser, starter beats, a track dock with one-knob effects and a Chord pad, a first-song tour and a Finish dock that saves the song as a file.
ui.fe.fmL: An imported project is saved as a .lynx file, and the original is never changed. After each import a report lists what was approximated or left out.
ui.fe.fmFlp: Channels, samples, patterns, arrangement, automation and mixer come in. FL Studio's native plugins play on LYNX SHARE's engines (see the list below). On export, what FL Studio does not have is rendered to audio or left out.
ui.fe.fmAls: Tracks, clips, mixer settings, automation, racks, Drum Racks and VST2 / VST3 plugins. Many of Live's own effects and instruments (EQ Eight, Compressor, Reverb, Auto Filter, Simpler, Drift and more) become LYNX SHARE's own; the others are dropped. On export, LYNX SHARE's own instruments and effects are not converted.
ui.fe.fmFlm: Arrangement, samples, drum kits, DW Sampler and DirectWave programs, the Slicer, MiniSynth, Transistor Bass, 3x Osc, GMSynth and SuperSaw, the effects, the automation and the chord sets. Other instruments play the built-in synth.
ui.fe.fmMid: As a new project, or into the current one from the Piano roll.
ui.fe.fmAud: WAV at 16-bit, 24-bit or 32-bit float. Stems: one file per mixer insert, per channel or per Playlist track.
ui.fe.synC: The built-in synth: 3 oscillators, a multimode filter with keytracking, FM and ring modulation, envelopes and 4 LFOs.
ui.fe.eqC: Facet EQ: 8 bands, cuts up to 96 dB/oct, dynamic bands and a pre/post analyser, at zero latency.
ui.fe.ins1: Sampler with zones, slices, time-stretch and disk streaming
ui.fe.ins2: LYNX Soundfont, an SF2 / SF3 player
ui.fe.ins3: Built-in drums: kick, snare, hat, clap
ui.fe.ins4: Note effects (sequencer, key mapper, keyboard splitter) and controllers (X-Y, envelope, voltage)
ui.fe.fx1: EQs, compressor with sidechain, limiter, gate
ui.fe.fx3: Vocoder, pitch correction, pitch and frequency shifters
ui.fe.fx4: Patcher: a node graph of effects, instruments and plugins
ui.fe.fx5: Hardware insert for outboard gear, with delay compensation

ui.fe.insL: LYNX SHARE has its own effects that play the role of widely used third-party plugins. If a project uses one of those plugins and it is not installed, the LYNX SHARE effect loads in its slot and the original's settings are kept for when it is back.

ui.fe.engP: The audio engine spreads channels and mixer tracks across CPU cores, skips channels that are silent and streams long audio files from disk. Measured against FL Studio 2026 on the developer's PC, it used 2.5 to 7 times less RAM and rendered the demo songs 2 to 3 times faster. The method and the numbers are in the benchmark notes; your results will differ.
ui.dlp.sub: Free, with no account, for Windows, macOS and Linux.
ui.dl.hwin: Windows 10 or 11, 64-bit. The installer needs no admin rights. The executable is not code-signed yet: if SmartScreen warns, choose More info → Run anyway.
ui.dl.portWinP: Unzip to any folder and open LYNX.exe.
ui.dl.store: Windows 10 / 11: also on the Microsoft Store, with automatic updates.
ui.dl.hmac: macOS 11 or newer, Apple Silicon or Intel. The app is not notarized by Apple yet: drag LYNX SHARE to Applications, then the first time right-click it → Open → Open (on macOS 15 or newer: try to open it once, then System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway). Or in Terminal: xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/LYNX.app
ui.dl.hlinux: Linux x86_64 with glibc 2.35 or newer (Ubuntu 22.04, Debian 12, Fedora 36 or newer). AppImage: chmod +x LYNX-*.AppImage, then run it (some distros need libfuse2). The .tar.gz has an install.sh that installs for your user with a menu entry.

ui.dlp.know1: LYNX SHARE is an alpha. It opens, plays and exports whole projects, but it has bugs. Save often, and keep a copy of anything you import from another program.
ui.dlp.know2: Installed versions offer new releases through an Update bar under the toolbar. The Microsoft Store version updates through the Store, and the AppImage through AppImageUpdate or Gear Lever.
ui.dlp.know3: Plugin formats differ per system: VST3 and CLAP everywhere, Audio Units on macOS, LV2 on Linux, VST2 on Windows and Linux. ASIO and the 32-bit plugin bridge are Windows-only.

ui.fix.sub: Complaints that come up again and again about DAWs, and what LYNX SHARE does about each one. Everything in the list is in the current release.
ui.fix.1.c: In most DAWs a third-party plugin runs inside the program. When the plugin crashes, the program goes with it, and so does anything you had not saved.
ui.fix.1.l: Turn on "Run plugins in a separate process" in Options › General settings, or choose it for one plugin from the menu of its window. A plugin that crashes then goes silent and the program keeps running. It is off by default, and such a plugin opens its editor in its own window. Even without it, a plugin that crashes while it plays is switched off and the program keeps running, on Windows, macOS and Linux. A plugin that crashed can be reloaded from its window, with its settings from the last save or backup, without reopening the project.
ui.fix.2.c: One broken plugin can freeze or crash the scan of a whole plugin folder, and you are left to find the culprit by hand.
ui.fix.2.l: Each plugin file is scanned in its own process. A file that crashes or takes too long is marked as failed and skipped from then on. In the Plugin manager you can right-click it and try again.
ui.fix.3.c: A timed backup that lands while the song is playing can make the audio stutter.
ui.fix.3.l: Backups wait while the song plays or while you play a MIDI keyboard, and none is written during a recording. After ten minutes without a backup one is made anyway. Both are settings in Options › General settings.
ui.fix.4.t: Finding your work after a crash
ui.fix.4.c: After a crash it is often unclear whether a backup exists and where it is.
ui.fix.4.l: A backup copy is saved every two minutes and the ten newest are kept for each project. After an unclean exit, the next start offers the newest one. File › Revert to last backup and File › Open autosave folder reach them at any time. File › Versions... lists a project's saved versions and backups in one window.
ui.fix.5.t: The idea you played without recording
ui.fix.5.c: The best take is often the one played before pressing record.
ui.fix.5.l: Capture MIDI (Ctrl+Shift+Alt+R) puts the notes you just played into the pattern. Tools › Audio logger keeps a rolling recording of the Master and is on by default.
ui.fix.27.t: A project that crashes while it opens
ui.fix.27.c: After a plugin update, a project can crash the DAW every time it loads, and the only way to find the culprit is to remove plugins one by one.
ui.fix.27.l: File › Open without third-party plugins... opens the project with every third-party plugin off and its settings kept. A window lists them, and Switch on brings them back one at a time, so the one that breaks the project shows itself.
ui.fix.28.t: Projects that live only on a server
ui.fix.28.c: Some online DAWs keep no copy of a project on your device. When the account, the connection or the service has a problem, the work is out of reach.
ui.fix.28.l: A LYNX SHARE project is a file on your own disk and the program works offline. Nothing is uploaded unless you send a project to someone or start a live session.
ui.fix.6.c: Many 64-bit DAWs no longer load 32-bit plugins, so older instruments and effects are lost.
ui.fix.6.l: On Windows, 32-bit VST2 and VST3 plugins run through a bridge that adds no latency. This is Windows only, and the plugin's editor opens in its own window.
ui.fix.7.c: Feeding one track into another track's compressor usually means building the route by hand in the mixer. In FL Studio that is several steps.
ui.fix.7.l: Effects with a side input have a "Sidechain from" picker that lists the inserts. Picking one makes the route. Third-party plugins with a second input get the same picker.
ui.fix.8.t: Which plugin is using the CPU
ui.fix.8.c: When the audio crackles it is hard to tell which plugin is responsible.
ui.fix.8.l: Tools › Plugin performance monitor lists every instrument and effect with its processing time now, on average and at its peak.
ui.fix.9.c: CLAP is a newer, open plugin format, and not every DAW loads it.
ui.fix.9.l: LYNX SHARE loads CLAP plugins on Windows, macOS and Linux, next to VST3. VST2, Audio Units and LV2 load on the systems that have them.
ui.fix.22.t: Heavy instruments that use up the computer
ui.fix.22.c: A project with many heavy instruments reaches the limit of the computer's memory and processor. Bouncing each one to audio by hand loses the way back.
ui.fix.22.l: Right-click a channel in the Channel rack and choose Freeze. The channel plays audio rendered from it and its instrument is unloaded, a third-party plugin included. Unfreeze brings back exactly what was there. Only instrument channels can be frozen, not mixer inserts.
ui.fix.29.c: A plugin window you are tweaking disappears behind the main window as soon as you click elsewhere.
ui.fix.29.l: A detached plugin window has Pin on top in its header and in its menu, and then stays above LYNX SHARE's other windows. It is not available for a plugin in a separate process.
ui.fix.30.t: Splitting a song into stems costs extra
ui.fix.30.c: Stem separation is in the most expensive edition of some DAWs and behind a membership in others.
ui.fix.30.l: Right-click an audio clip in the Playlist and choose Extract stems from sample: drums, bass, vocals and the other instruments come out on new Playlist tracks. It runs on your own computer; the model is downloaded once, after asking.
ui.fix.31.t: AI tools that send your project away
ui.fix.31.c: Assistants built into DAWs upload project data to the maker's servers, and it is not always clear what is sent.
ui.fix.31.l: Convert to MIDI and Extract stems from sample run on your own computer. LYNX SHARE has no built-in assistant and no account, and sends no project data unless you start a live session, send a project or agree to send a crash report.
ui.fix.10.c: FL Studio and Ableton Live cannot open each other's projects. Moving a song usually means exporting audio and starting again.
ui.fix.10.l: File › Open reads .flp, .als (Live 11 and 12) and .flm. File › Export writes an FL Studio project or an Ableton Live set. A report lists what was approximated. In Live sets, Live's own devices are not converted.
ui.fix.11.t: Missing samples after a project moves
ui.fix.11.c: A project opened on another computer, or after its files were moved, loses its samples and gives little help in finding them.
ui.fix.11.l: The Missing files window opens after loading. It can search a folder, locate one file or skip it. Help › Missing files opens it again.
ui.fix.12.t: Routing that breaks when mixer tracks move
ui.fix.12.c: In FL Studio, moving or deleting mixer tracks can leave sends and sidechains pointing at the wrong track.
ui.fix.12.l: Moving, inserting or deleting mixer tracks keeps sends, sidechains, automation and MIDI links on the track they belong to. Links to a track you delete can be kept and shown greyed, and the inserts can be put in the order of the Playlist's tracks.
ui.fix.13.t: Recorded notes you cannot see until you stop
ui.fix.13.c: In FL Studio, the notes you are recording do not appear in the Playlist until the recording ends.
ui.fix.13.l: The take is drawn in the Playlist and the Piano roll while you record.
ui.fix.14.t: Stems with the bus effects baked in
ui.fix.14.c: Stem exports often carry send and bus effects that the person receiving them does not want.
ui.fix.14.l: The export window has "One per channel, instruments only (no sends or buses)".
ui.fix.15.c: Reaching a streaming target such as -14 LUFS takes several trial exports in a DAW that has no loudness target.
ui.fix.15.l: File › Export › Master (Ctrl+Alt+M) masters the song to the LUFS target you choose, on your own computer. A loudness meter beside the Master (off by default) shows short-term and integrated LUFS and the true peak. View › Reference match... measures a finished song you like and matches the Master's tone and loudness to it.
ui.fix.16.t: Small things FL Studio users keep asking for
ui.fix.16.c: Finer knob movements, a gain-reduction meter on the mixer strip and tools to clean up unused patterns are long-standing requests.
ui.fix.16.l: Ctrl+drag moves a control finely and Ctrl+Shift+drag a hundred times finer. Mixer strips show gain reduction for LYNX SHARE's own dynamics effects. The pattern menu has Select unused, Delete unused patterns and Merge identical patterns.
ui.fix.23.t: Audio that is not in time
ui.fix.23.c: A recorded loop or a sample at another tempo has to be lined up with the project by hand.
ui.fix.23.l: Auto-warp finds the beat of an audio clip and locks it to the project's tempo. In the audio editor's warp lane you can add, move and remove the markers yourself.
ui.fix.24.t: Getting the notes out of a recording
ui.fix.24.c: Turning a hummed melody or a drum loop into notes usually takes another program or an online service.
ui.fix.24.l: Convert to MIDI turns the melody, the harmony or the drums of an audio clip into a new pattern. It runs on your own computer.
ui.fix.25.t: Undo keys that differ between programs
ui.fix.25.c: In FL Studio, Ctrl+Z undoes and redoes only the last step. People who come from other programs expect it to keep stepping back.
ui.fix.25.l: By default the keys are FL Studio's: Ctrl+Z undoes and redoes the last step, and Ctrl+Alt+Z steps back through the history. "Alternate undo mode" in the general settings swaps the two.
ui.fix.26.t: Too many windows on the first day
ui.fix.26.c: A full DAW shows a beginner dozens of windows and controls before the first sound.
ui.fix.26.l: View › Layout style › Simple workflow shows one window with the tracks and the timeline. A new track is a voice, an instrument, a sampler or a starter beat in one click, and the other windows stay one click away. The setup wizard offers it at the first start.
ui.fix.32.t: Hearing yourself late while you record
ui.fix.32.c: An effect that adds latency on the track you record through, or on the Master, makes you hear your own voice or playing late.
ui.fix.32.l: Right-click the record button, or open Mixer › Disk recording, and turn on Low latency while recording. Effects that add latency on an armed or monitored insert, and on its way to the Master, are bypassed until the insert is disarmed or its monitoring is turned off. What is recorded does not change. It is off by default.
ui.fix.33.t: Loops that preview at the wrong tempo
ui.fix.33.c: Auditioning a loop in the browser plays it at its own tempo, so you cannot tell whether it fits the song.
ui.fix.33.l: Turn on Preview in time in the Browser's menu: loops then play at the project's tempo and on the beat. It is off by default.
ui.fix.34.t: Notes that slip out of key
ui.fix.34.c: Drawing or moving notes by hand easily lands them outside the song's scale.
ui.fix.34.l: Choose a scale in the Piano roll and turn on Snap to scale: new and moved notes, and notes coming in from a MIDI keyboard, land on the scale.
ui.fix.35.t: Exporting every section of a song, again and again
ui.fix.35.c: Rendering the intro, verse and drop as separate files, with the same settings each time, means setting up the export window over and over.
ui.fix.35.l: The Export window has One file per marker section, which renders each section between Playlist markers to its own file, also with stems. Its settings can be saved as named presets.
ui.fix.36.t: Sends that move with the fader
ui.fix.36.c: Headphone mixes and some effects need a send that keeps its level when the track's fader moves.
ui.fix.36.l: Right-click a send knob or a route arrow in the Mixer and choose Pre-fader send. FL Studio's post-fader send stays the default.
ui.fix.37.t: No way to comp the best take
ui.fix.37.c: Building one take from the best parts of several means cutting, moving and muting clips by hand.
ui.fix.37.l: Loop recording keeps every pass on its own Playlist track in a group. Right-click a track of the group and choose Comp these takes: a comp track is added above them, a drag across a take sends that part to it, with short crossfades where the take changes, and Flatten comp keeps what plays.
ui.fix.38.t: Recordings that land a little late
ui.fix.38.c: A take lands a few milliseconds behind the beat, and it is hard to tell whether the DAW or the audio interface is to blame.
ui.fix.38.l: Recordings are placed using the latency the audio driver reports. For an exact figure, Options › Audio settings... › Measure the round trip plays clicks from an output to an input through a cable or a loopback and times their way back. With Use the measured round trip on, takes are placed by that figure, kept for that device, sample rate and buffer size.
ui.fix.17.c: FL Studio and Ableton Live are not made for Linux.
ui.fix.17.l: LYNX SHARE has a native Linux build (AppImage and tar.gz) with PipeWire, JACK and ALSA, and loads VST3, CLAP, LV2 and VST2 plugins there. It needs X11 or XWayland.
ui.fix.18.c: Trial versions often cannot reopen the projects you saved, and many programs need an account or a subscription.
ui.fix.18.l: LYNX SHARE is free and open source under the AGPL-3.0, with no account. Saving and reopening have no limit. Crash reports are sent only if you agree, and the update check sends nothing about you.

ui.faq.a1: Yes. It is free software under the GNU Affero General Public License v3.0 (AGPL-3.0). You may use, study, modify and redistribute it. Anyone who distributes a modified version must publish its source code under the same licence.
ui.faq.q2: Which systems does it run on?
ui.faq.a2: Windows 10 and 11 (64-bit), macOS 11 or newer (Apple Silicon and Intel) and Linux x86_64 with glibc 2.35 or newer (Ubuntu 22.04, Debian 12, Fedora 36 or newer). The files are on the download page.
ui.faq.q3: Is this FL Studio, or made by Image-Line?
ui.faq.a3: No. LYNX SHARE is an independent program with an FL Studio-style workflow. FL Studio's behaviour and file format were studied clean-room, no Image-Line code was copied, and LYNX SHARE is not affiliated with Image-Line.
ui.faq.q4: Does it open my FL Studio projects, and what is lost?
ui.faq.a4: File › Open... reads .flp files: channels, samples, patterns, arrangements, automation, the Mixer and third-party plugins you have installed. FL Studio's native plugins play on recreated engines, most of them exact or near-exact and a few approximate. FLEX packs are never opened. An import report lists what was approximated or left out. See Coming from FL Studio.
ui.faq.q5: Does it open Ableton Live sets?
ui.faq.a5: Yes, sets saved by Live 11 and 12 (.als): tracks, clips, mixer settings, automation and VST2 or VST3 plugins. Racks and Drum Racks come in with their chains and macros, many of Live's own effects and instruments (EQ Eight, Compressor, Reverb, Auto Filter, Simpler, Drift and more) become LYNX SHARE's own, and the others are dropped and listed in the import report. See Coming from Ableton Live.
ui.faq.q6: Does it open FL Studio Mobile projects?
ui.faq.a6: Partly. A .flm opens with its arrangement, samples, drum kits, DW Sampler and DirectWave programs, the Slicer, the MiniSynth, Transistor Bass, 3x Osc, GMSynth and SuperSaw instruments, FL Studio Mobile's effects, its automation and its chord sets. Other instruments play the built-in synth.
ui.faq.q7: Can I send a project back to FL Studio or Live?
ui.faq.a7: Yes. File › Export › FL Studio project... writes a .flp, and File › Export › Ableton Live set (.als)... writes a set for Live 12 or Live 11. What the other program does not have is rendered to audio or left out, and a report says which. The limits are on the File formats page.
ui.faq.a8: VST3 and CLAP plugins load on every system. VST2 loads on Windows and Linux, Audio Units on macOS and LV2 on Linux. On Windows, 32-bit VST2 and VST3 plugins run through a bridge. See Plugins.
ui.faq.a9: It is an alpha. It opens, plays and exports whole projects, but it is not yet a replacement for the DAW you rely on every day. Save often and report what breaks.
ui.faq.q10: Why does Windows or macOS warn when I open it?
ui.faq.a10: The Windows executable is not code-signed yet, so SmartScreen may warn: click More info, then Run anyway. The macOS app is not notarized by Apple: right-click it and choose Open the first time. The steps are on the Troubleshooting page.
ui.faq.a11: There is no telemetry, analytics, account or licence check. It checks GitHub for a new version (you can turn this off in Settings › General › Updates), and it sends a crash report only if you agree each time or set it to always send. It also connects when you ask for a stem model download or take part in a live online session. The privacy policy has the details.
ui.faq.a12: When a newer version exists, a bar under the toolbar offers Update. The Windows installer version installs it over itself. The portable and macOS versions save the new file to your Downloads folder. The Linux AppImage updates through AppImageUpdate or Gear Lever. The Microsoft Store version is updated by the Store and has no Update button. Release notes are on the updates page.
ui.faq.q13: Which languages does the interface have?
ui.faq.a13: Fifteen: English, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, Dutch, French, German, Indonesian, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Polish, Brazilian Portuguese, Russian, Spanish and Turkish.
ui.faq.q14: How do I report a bug or contribute?
ui.faq.a14: Open an issue at github.com/Ka1-S/LYNX-SHARE/issues, or use Help › Report a problem... inside the program. The source code is in the same repository, and pull requests from contributors have been merged in past releases.
ui.faq.q15: Is there a simpler layout for beginners?
ui.faq.a15: Yes. View › Layout style › Simple workflow shows one window with the tracks and the timeline, and the setup wizard offers it at the first start. The Pattern workflow stays the default, and the same menu switches back. See Simple layout.
ui.faq.q16: Will an update change how my projects sound?
ui.faq.a16: No, not on purpose. When one of LYNX SHARE's effects is refitted to sound closer to the plugin it is modelled on, the new behaviour is a switch (Law: Classic | Measured): new instances use it, and projects and presets saved earlier keep the old one. Only real fixes, such as a limiter that went over its ceiling, change a saved project, and the release notes list them.
ui.faq.q17: Can I use FL Studio's own plugins in LYNX SHARE?
ui.faq.a17: Yes, through the FL Studio plugin that comes with FL Studio. FL Studio installs itself as a plugin too: FL Studio VSTi and FL Studio VSTi (Multi) (VST2) on Windows, and an Audio Unit on macOS. Put it on a channel in LYNX SHARE and FL Studio runs inside it, with its Channel rack, Patcher, Sytrus, Harmor and the other plugins your FL Studio licence covers. It needs FL Studio installed and your own licence. LYNX SHARE does not load FL Studio's plugin files directly, because they are made to run only inside FL Studio. If an older version of LYNX SHARE listed the FL Studio plugin as Failed to load, right-click it in Options › Plugin manager... and choose Try again (scan this file now).
